root_cause.text: The RLIMIT_MEMLOCK accounting for MSG_ZEROCOPY pinned pages uses iter->count after it has been consumed by __zerocopy_sg_from_iter(), causing the last skb to have a zero count and bypass the limit enforcement.
root_cause.evidence: CVE description states "on the last skb, iter->count will be 0, skipping the RLIMIT_MEMLOCK enforcement." The patch replaces iter->count with an explicit pkt_len parameter in msg_zerocopy_realloc() to use the original total message size.

The msghdr pointer is used in the zero-copy path; its iter member is the source of the count that gets consumed, leading to zero pkt_len.

The pkt_len parameter is directly passed to msg_zerocopy_realloc for RLIMIT_MEMLOCK accounting. If pkt_len is zero because it was derived from iter->count after consumption by __zerocopy_sg_from_iter(), the limit enforcement is bypassed, causing the vulnerability.
